text: In Hamiltonian mechanics the Hamiltonian is defined as H = T − V, the kinetic minus the potential energy.
explanation: False. H = T − V is the Lagrangian; for a standard system the Hamiltonian is H = T + V, the total energy expressed in terms of (q, p) via the Legendre transform H = p·q̇ − L. Confusing the sign — L = T − V versus H = T + V — is a common error.
